intro_en: Sahih al-Bukhari opens with the Book of Revelation because revelation is the source of all matters of religion, placed before faith, knowledge, and every other book. It begins with the hadith of intentions — reminding compiler and reader that deeds are judged by intention.

sources.name: Qari Muhammad Tayyib, 'The Last Hadith of Sahih Bukhari' (Khatm-e-Bukhari lecture, 11 July 1977; English translation)
Mahmud Hasan Deobandi, Al-Abwab wa al-Tarajim, pp. 16-17 (quoted on tohed.com)
Foreword to 'Sahih Al-Bukhari: The Book of Faith' explained by Shaykh Abdul Aziz Ar-Rajhi (Abu Aaliyah)
Shaykh Yasir Qadhi / AlMaghrib Institute, 'An Introduction to the Sahih of Imam Al-Bukhari' (January 2012)

intro_en: The Book of Belief follows Revelation because faith is the foundation on which all actions are built — no deed is valid without it. The book establishes that iman combines inward affirmation with outward speech and actions, presenting the position of Ahl al-Sunnah on the nature of faith.

sources.name: Qari Muhammad Tayyib, 'The Last Hadith of Sahih Bukhari' (Khatm-e-Bukhari lecture, 11 July 1977; English translation)
Foreword to 'Sahih Al-Bukhari: The Book of Faith' explained by Shaykh Abdul Aziz Ar-Rajhi (Abu Aaliyah)

intro_en: The Book of Knowledge comes after Revelation and Belief because knowledge must precede action: once a person has faith, they need to learn how to fulfill its requirements. The book covers the virtue of knowledge, its methods, and the etiquette of teaching and learning.

sources.name: Shaykh Yasir Qadhi / AlMaghrib Institute, 'An Introduction to the Sahih of Imam Al-Bukhari' (January 2012)
Qari Muhammad Tayyib, 'The Last Hadith of Sahih Bukhari' (Khatm-e-Bukhari lecture, 11 July 1977; English translation)

intro_en: Bukhari devotes a distinct book to the Witr prayer, giving it headings of its own rather than subsuming it under the chapters on Tahajjud and voluntary prayer. The book sets out the rulings of Witr.

sources.name: Fath al-Bari — Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, Kitab al-Witr (IslamWeb digital library)
Umdat al-Qari — Badr al-Din al-Ayni, Kitab al-Witr (Shamela digital library)

intro_en: Bukhari's Book of Tahajjud gathers the reports on night prayer; his aim is to establish the legitimacy of night prayer without addressing its legal ruling.

sources.name: Fath al-Bari — Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani (IslamWeb digital library)
Umdat al-Qari — Badr al-Din al-Ayni (Shamela digital library)

intro_en: Bukhari's Book of Funerals (Janaza) sets out the rulings of funerals — a prayer with no bowing or prostration — placed after the prayer chapters and before the Book of Zakat.

sources.name: Fath al-Bari — Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani (IslamWeb digital library)
Umdat al-Qari — Badr al-Din al-Ayni (Shamela digital library)
Fath al-Bari — Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani (IslamWeb digital library)

intro_en: Bukhari's Book of Zakat sets out the rulings of Zakat, the third pillar of Islam.

sources.name: Fath al-Bari — Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani (IslamWeb digital library)
Umdat al-Qari — Badr al-Din al-Ayni (Shamela digital library)

intro_en: Bukhari devotes the Book of Hajj to explaining Hajj — purposeful intent in language, and in law the journey to the Sacred House with specific rites. He places it after the Book of Zakat and before the Book of Fasting.

sources.name: Fath al-Bari — Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, Kitab al-Hajj (IslamWeb digital library)
Umdat al-Qari — Badr al-Din al-Ayni, Kitab al-Hajj (Shamela digital library)

intro_en: Kitab Bad' al-Khalq — 'The Beginning of Creation' — is the book on the origination of creation: that is, the created beings.

sources.name: Fath al-Bari (Ibn Hajar) via Islamweb
'Umdat al-Qari (al-'Ayni) via Taghrib mirror

intro_en: Kitab al-Maghazi is the book of the Prophet's military expeditions. 'Maghazi' is the plural of 'maghzan', and 'ghazw' means setting out to fight the enemy. Its subject is the Prophet's campaigns against the disbelievers — whether he led them himself or sent armies under his command — encompassing expeditions into enemy lands as well as battles fought where the enemy came, such as Uhud and al-Khandaq. Bukhari does not separate maghazi from saraya (the smaller expeditions he dispatched): he includes the saraya and the bu'uth (dispatches) in this book as well.

intro_en: The Book of Divorce extends beyond the act of terminating a marriage to related questions of waiting periods and other connected consequences of separation.

sources.name: Scott C. Lucas, "Divorce, Hadith-Scholar Style: From al-Darimi to al-Tirmidhi," Journal of Islamic Studies 19:3 (2008), 325-368. DOI 10.1093/jis/etn005 (author-posted copy).

intro_en: Bukhari's Book of Medicine (Kitab al-Tibb) gathers hadiths on the treatment of illness, including methods of treatment.
